M.units: direct-tap units (unit cluster gain); delays in integer device samples from tap 0; mono in, (L, R) out; the input impulse at sample 0
M.signal_path: static/reference path: input -> tap injection -> four coupled lines (filter G_j in the feedback, delay P_j, coupling F) -> sum -> diffuser (all-passes, the last damped by b) -> output kernel; the direct path (four taps per channel) adds in parallel. The plugin's time-varying path is the read-out form in modulation.application: the diffused input feeds the lines and each channel's taps read u_i; with theta = 0 the two forms are equivalent (ml_variance.core, about -174 dB)
M.measurement_side: not in this spec and not in the reference IRs: the 100 Hz-10 kHz analysis band (ml.BAND), the capture clock ratio and shift (ml_lines.warp), the per-capture cluster and reverb gains, the file fades and usable ends, and the chain3 capture-chain kernel. The plugin's own analogue chain and time variance are separate and follow this spec

baseline.damping: ML_BREFIT=steps, analysis/ml_lines/b_steps_ml.json (one table for M and L)

value.form: x_j[n] = t_j[n] + G_j * (sum_k F[j,k] x_k)[n - P_j]; the four filters are in settings.<key>.lines (gain, shelf DC gain, HF pole), the shelf pole is the S law's a = 0.916883 and the shelf's Nyquist gain is 1 (the HF one-pole's is (1 - p) / (1 + p))
value.filter_form: G_j = gain * (b0 + b1 z^-1)/(1 - a z^-1) * (1 - p)/(1 - p z^-1), b0 = (r0 (1 - a) + (1 + a))/2, b1 = (r0 (1 - a) - (1 + a))/2, r0 = shelf_dc; p = hf_pole and p = 0 bypasses the HF one-pole
value.law: S's line law at the line's own length: g = 10^(-3 P / (fs hi RT)), shelf DC = 10^(-3 P / fs (1/(dc RT) - 1/(hi RT))), HF one-pole at f_ref with T = 10^(-3 P / (fs RT) k (1/HF_e - 1)), HF_e = max(HF, HFRT_MIN x program scale / RT); the DC floor lifts g by 10^(-beta lift / 20) and sets the shelf to dc_min / g when g r0 < DC_MIN; the p_max cap is used only when the pole curve is off (ML_POLE_CURVE=0) or a non-default p_max is passed (the adopted curve maps and caps at its own knots / DROP_BACK). L's RT 2.2 floor 0.40 and HFRT_MIN 0.12 x the program scale (x2 M, x4 L)

lines.label: S at the library's steps / H between them (LF log-interpolated between S's steps; RT and HF continuous; b from the nearest (RT, HF) cell)

value.form: y = h * [C + D * 1^T (I - Lambda F)^-1 T], Lambda = diag(G_j z^-P_j); F is orthogonal (the bipartite matrix, entries +-1/sqrt(2))

value.gains: unit; AMPL scales the cluster only (the pairs measure that the reverb tails are identical after one gain); the absolute AMPL scale is the plugin's calibration (H)
value.onset: tap 0 at sample k_h after the output kernel (causal), not at sample 0

value.note: the first-pass/read taps, one sum per channel and line; fitted on 6 training settings, held out by setting and AMPL

value.damping: the last all-pass's two-tap loop filter (1 - b) + b z^-1, b per setting in settings.<key>.b; the step comes from the setting's (RT, HF) cell in analysis/ml_lines/b_steps.json, and the value from the shared table in analysis/ml_lines/b_steps_ml.json
value.form: all-passes H = (-g + z^-M F)/(1 - g z^-M F) in series

value.note: causal: the kernel's centre tap k_h lands at the cluster tap 0's time, so the reference IRs place cluster tap 0 at sample k_h

value.measured_rms: 0.13 rad (0.11-0.144, bootstrap over groups), against Tomkin's AMPL pairs with 12 evenly spaced sim phases (analysis/plugin_check/theta_depth.json, ml_structure.md 9.8); the earlier 0.15 (9.7) came from 6 random phases per group that happened to understate the decorrelation
value.form: theta(t) = amplitude sin(2 pi rate t + phase); phase random per capture; a sine shape is H, the depth is S
value.coupling: one angle of both 2x2 blocks: F(theta) = F R(theta) per block, R = [[cos, -sin], [sin, cos]]; F stays orthogonal
value.application: read-out form: u_i = x + sum_j F(theta)_ji v_j, v_j = G_j u_j delayed P_j; each channel's taps read u_i. With theta = 0 it reproduces the static network to about -100 dB (ml_variance.py)
value.status: always on in the plugin; the static reference IRs are theta = 0. Check the moving part statistically: Tomkin's AMPL pairs decorrelate like theta renders from the first recirculation to 2-4 s (ml_structure.md §9.5-9.7)

modulation.label: S (rate, depth, one angle) / H (sine shape and phase)

AMPL.value: the cluster only; the reverb is fixed (the AMPL pairs are repeat captures after one gain). The library steps: [10, 60, 99]
AMPL.label: S (cluster-only) / H (scale)

DELAY.value: a pure delay of the whole output; the library is all DELAY 0
DELAY.label: H

LOW_PASS.value: the panel's LOW PASS has no varying files in the library; response unknown
LOW_PASS.label: H

not_resolved: theta's shape and phase (the sine is H; the 0.13 rad rms depth is S)
the LOW PASS response and DELAY steps (no library data)
the law between the library's LF / RT / HF steps (H: LF log-interpolated, RT / HF continuous; b nearest (RT, HF) cell)
the absolute AMPL scale (per-capture gains are fitted, so the model does not fix it)

references.note: device rate (the exact device_rate_hz; the WAV header is the integer wav_sample_rate_hz), float32, (L, R), input impulse at sample 0, direct-tap units, the output kernel causal so cluster tap 0 is at sample k_h. A port must null these sample for sample (float precision). They are the static (theta = 0) network without the measurement band, where simulate() is at -130 dB or better against ml_lines.Model.parts
